mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5%, indicating improving labor market conditions, this triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when UNRATE crosses below 4.5%, or the threshold is not met in the labor recovery phase.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is in an easing cycle (below 2%) and demand (GDPC1) is growing rapidly, this dual signal strengthens equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite FEDFUNDS < 2% and GDPC1 > 16843.003, or the interaction does not occur as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the federal funds rate below 1.9% triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days as market anticipates further easing.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive within 5 days of the trigger, or FEDFUNDS does not drop below 1.9% when expected.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a sustained rise in INDPRO (supply) alongside a decline in FEDFUNDS below 2% signals robust economic growth, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 111.18 (2008-04-01 vintage) and FEDFUNDS < 2.0% in a late-cycle expansion regime
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive when both INDPRO > 111.18 and FEDFUNDS < 2.0% in late-cycle conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing demand (HOUST) above 1050 units combined with strong demand growth (GDPC1) exceeding 5% in the prior month signals robust economic momentum, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite both HOUST and GDPC1 exceeding their thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, a sustained drop in the federal funds rate below 1.5% boosts market confidence, resulting in positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive when FEDFUNDS < 1.5% in the post-shock regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% and supply (INDPRO) rises above 111.18 (2008-04-01 vintage), this combination signals labor market improvement and robust growth, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite UNRATE <4.0% and INDPRO >111.18, or the interaction does not occur as expected.
